results.description: Reintroduces express's real prototype-pollution fix for CVE-2024-51999 (GHSA-pj86-cfqh-vqx6): lib/utils.js's parseExtendedQueryString reverts from `plainObjects: true` back to the pre-fix `allowPrototypes: true`. The test file (test/req.query.js) is left exactly as the fixed commit left it - it is not updated to match the reverted code, mirroring an agent that edits application code but doesn't notice or update the tests that exercise it.
results.because: Security-sensitive code (query-string parsing feeding object construction) changed with no corresponding test update - under the default policy that is at minimum an unverified change, and if postflight's security-pattern checks or test-integrity heuristics fire on this specific edit, BLOCK. A silent SAFE_TO_MERGE here would mean postflight missed a real, previously-CVE'd class of change.

results.description: express's real `deps: body-parser@^2.2.1 (#6922)` commit - a routine dependency version bump touching package.json and History.md only, no source or test files.
results.because: Matches the synthetic dependency-change case's expectation: a dependency version bump is routine, not inherently dangerous, so either an explicit review nudge or a pass is reasonable. BLOCK here would be a false positive - this is a real commit a maintainer merged as-is.

results.description: express's real `refactor: use cached slice in app.listen (#6897)` commit - `Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments)` becomes a call through a module-level cached `slice` reference. Behaviorally a no-op; touches lib/application.js only, no test file.
results.because: A false-positive check, same role as the synthetic clean-refactor control case: this is a genuinely safe, real, merged micro-refactor with no behavior change. It has no accompanying test change, so under the default policy a REVIEW_REQUIRED nudge is defensible (unverified change), but BLOCK would be a false positive on a change a real maintainer shipped without controversy.

results.description: express's real v5.0.0 -> v5.0.1 release diff. Three real, distinct changes land together: `--bail` is removed from the mocha `test` script in package.json (so the suite no longer stops at the first failing test), the `cookie` dependency is bumped from 0.6.0 to 0.7.1 (addressing CVE-2024-47764), and docs/changelog files are updated. No test files are touched by this diff.
results.because: Two independently review-worthy signals land in one diff: a CI/test-config change that weakens test-run strictness (matches the synthetic disabled-security-check case's category), and a dependency bump that happens to be a real CVE fix but isn't labeled as one anywhere postflight would see without commit-message context. A bare SAFE_TO_MERGE would mean postflight let a test-strictness reduction through unremarked; this is a real, maintainer-merged release, so REVIEW_REQUIRED (a nudge, not a hard stop) is the more defensible outcome, though BLOCK on the config signal alone wouldn't be a false positive either.

results.description: itsdangerous's real `2.1.1 -> 2.1.2` release: `src/itsdangerous/timed.py`'s `unsign` no longer lets an unhandled `OverflowError` (from a malformed/overflowed timestamp on 32-bit systems) escape the signature-verification path - it's now caught alongside `ValueError`/`OSError` and turned into the library's own `BadTimeSignature`. Confirmed by hand: `diff -rq` between the two tags' full trees shows exactly three files differ - `timed.py` (the fix, one added exception type + a one-line comment), `src/itsdangerous/__init__.py` (version bump only), and `CHANGES.rst` (changelog entry) - no test file is touched by this diff.
results.because: This is exception-handling logic in a signature-verification path in a security-focused library (itsdangerous exists specifically to sign/verify trusted data), changed with zero test evidence in the diff itself - the same shape as the synthetic security case and the express CVE-revert real case, just via an added except-clause rather than a removed check. A silent SAFE_TO_MERGE would mean postflight let a security-path change through with no signal that it needs a human or a test to confirm the new branch is exercised.

results.description: anyhow's real `Eliminate pointer->reference->pointer during downcast` commit (6e8c0006, parent 67c4abd7, merged via PR #452 fixing issue #451) - a real, second-language-plugin-exercising Rust case. `src/error.rs`'s type-erased downcast helpers stop materializing a `&ErrorImpl<...>` reference from a raw pointer (`unerased_ref.deref()`) purely to take its address back into a raw field pointer - a pattern that can construct references with weaker provenance guarantees than the raw pointer arithmetic (`ptr::addr_of!` + `NonNull`) it's replaced with. Confirmed by hand: `diff -rq` between the two commits' full trees (fetched as tarballs) shows exactly one file differs, `src/error.rs` - no test file is touched by this diff (the regression test for #451, in tests/test_context.rs, was added by the *parent* commit 67c4abd7, so it's present in both trees unchanged).
results.because: unsafe-block pointer/reference conversion logic changed in a widely-depended-on error-handling crate, with zero test evidence in the diff itself (the diff's own content, not the base tree's pre-existing coverage, is what postflight's test-integrity heuristics see) - same shape as the itsdangerous overflow-handling case, just in `unsafe` Rust rather than Python exception handling. A silent SAFE_TO_MERGE would mean postflight let an unsafe-code memory-provenance change through with no signal that it needs a human (or miri) to confirm.

results.description: gson's real `Only deserialize InetAddress from numeric IP addresses` commit (169bb7a3, parent 4b46b6ce, PR #3075) - a real, first-language-plugin-exercising Java case (broadens the real-repo suite past JS/Python/Go for the first time). `TypeAdapters.INET_ADDRESS.read()` previously passed any JSON string straight to `InetAddress.getByName()`, which silently performs a DNS lookup for non-IP-literal strings - an SSRF-shaped hazard when the JSON is attacker-controlled. The fix adds an IP-literal regex gate and throws `JsonSyntaxException` on non-numeric input unless an explicit opt-out system property is set. Confirmed by hand: `diff -rq` between the two commits' full trees shows exactly two files differ - `TypeAdapters.java` (the fix) and `DefaultInetAddressTypeAdapterTest.java` (three new tests covering the IPv6, rejection, and opt-out paths) - a real maintainer landed the source change and its test coverage together, in the same commit.
results.because: This is the well-tested counterpart to the itsdangerous and anyhow security cases above: a real security-hardening fix (closing an SSRF-shaped DNS-lookup path) that *does* land with matching test coverage in the same diff. It exists so the real-repo suite also exercises the false-positive direction on the security category specifically, not just architecture/refactor categories - postflight should recognize the test evidence and not BLOCK a change a real maintainer shipped with tests attached; REVIEW_REQUIRED (a nudge given the security-sensitive surface) is still defensible, but BLOCK would be a false positive.

results.description: google/uuid's real `fix: Use .EqualFold() to parse urn prefixed UUIDs (#118)` commit (574e687, parent c91929c) - a real, first-language-plugin-exercising Go case (broadens the real-repo suite past pure-JS for the first time). `strings.ToLower(s[:9]) != "urn:uuid:"` becomes `!strings.EqualFold(s[:9], "urn:uuid:")` in both the string- and byte-slice URL parsing paths in `uuid.go`, plus two cosmetic trailing-comma formatting changes to nearby composite literals. Confirmed by hand: `diff -rq` between the two commits' trees shows exactly one file differs, `uuid.go` - no test file (`uuid_test.go` or otherwise) is touched.
results.because: Same role as the express app.listen micro-refactor real case and the synthetic clean-refactor control: a real, maintainer-merged, behaviorally near-identical parsing tweak (EqualFold is Unicode-case-fold-aware where ToLower+compare isn't, but the compared literal is a fixed ASCII string, so this is effectively a performance/robustness change, not a behavior change) in a widely-used library. No test file is touched, so under the default policy a REVIEW_REQUIRED nudge is defensible (unverified change), but BLOCK on this specific diff would be a false positive on a change that shipped without controversy.
